If  I were  to  say  that  I have  read  this  book  of  stories  (or  tales)  by 
VIr.  Dewi  Singh  Khongdup  and  found  it  entertaining,  I would  be 
telling  the  truth  no  doubt,  but  certainly  not  the  whole  truth.  Are 
there  stories  which  are  not  entertaining  in  their  own  way?  It  is  the 
quality,  it  is  the  intensity,  of  the  entertainment  depending  on  the 
manner  in  which  the  stary  has  been  told,  that  matters;  and  it  is  the 
manner  in  which  Mr.  Khongdup  tells  his  stories  that  has  given  the 
book  a pride  of  place  well  above  the  ordinary,  for  it  is  truly  more 
than  entertaining. 

Faiiy  tales  and  folk  tales  exist  in  every  language,  but  this 
creation  of  new  tales  by  Mr.  Khongdup  is  a wonderfully  clever  and 
creditable  performance.  The  conversation  pieces  put  into  the  mouths 
of  the  characters,  be  they  quadrupeds  or  bipeds,  are  always  refresh- 
ing, at  times  brilliantly  witty,  and,  where  you  least  expect  it,  the 
subtle  humour  woven  into  a harmless  looking  passage  explodes  with 
a bang,  and  the  reader  also  literally  explodes  with  uncontrollable 
laughter. 

1 hail  this  book  of  stories  by  Mr.  Khongdup  as  a great  and 
valuable  contribution  to  Khasi  Literature  and  I hope  readers  will 
derive  the  same  immense  pleasure  reading  it  as  1 have  done. 

S.  J.  Duncan 

Pheridale,  Nongkseh, 

Upper  Shillong,

The  25th  August,  1967
